cohort: The study included first-time mothers with Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA) who delivered between 1983 and 2010, and a 4:1 matched control group of first-time mothers without JIA.
finding: Mothers with JIA were at higher risk for anaesthetic complications, postpartum haemorrhage, and thromboembolism, but at lower risk for obstetrical trauma and newly developing depression in the first year postpartum.
